## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`--exclude` needs to read its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, because the project's flag policy requires this for every new flag under `cli/`. The flag's filtering logic itself is correct and covered by the added tests (read, not run).

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py`. `collect()` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped file. The pull request also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds parser, collection and end-to-end archive tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and adds a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Take the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src`, the `.log` files are still archived, because `--exclude` uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. This breaks the rule in `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that pass options through the environment cannot exclude files, contrary to the project's flag contract. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")` (decide and document how it splits into several patterns), list the variable in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` to cover the variable.
